objective: Give overlay/ a packaging step that produces a runnable Windows x86-64 Electron app for a machine with no npm, no Electron and no compiler. Today overlay/package.json has build/start/test/test:ui/typecheck and nothing that emits an installable artifact, which is the whole reason the overlay is proven end-to-end (TASK-210-S6, main 1846df2) and still in nobody's hands. Add a devDependency on @electron/packager (pinned), a packaging entrypoint overlay/package.mjs, and an `npm run package:win` script that first runs the existing build and then emits overlay/dist-win/PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay-win32-x64/PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay.exe. The artifact's directory and executable name are a CONTRACT: packaging/launch.py (TASK-215-S2) and scripts/package_mvp_windows.ps1 (TASK-215-S3) both hardcode them, so export them as constants from package.mjs and pin them in a test. Ship only what the app needs at runtime: esbuild already bundles src/ and web/src/ into dist/, so the packaged app is dist/ + package.json and nothing else.
constraints: The artifact NAME is a cross-stage contract. Export OUT_DIR ('dist-win'), APP_NAME ('PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay') and the resulting relative exe path from package.mjs, and assert them in overlay/test/packageWindows.test.ts. Two later stages hardcode 'overlay/PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay.exe' inside the bundle; renaming it silently breaks the player's launch.

Do NOT set an icon, a win32metadata block, or any executable version/description rewrite. Those invoke rcedit, which needs wine when packaging from Linux, and they buy nothing for a test build. Keep the packager options to platform/arch/dir/out/asar/overwrite/ignore.

`npm run package:win` DOWNLOADS the Electron win32-x64 binary (~100 MB) on first run. The required checks must therefore NOT run the packager: test the resolved option object and the exported constants, not the download. The real run is proven by pasted evidence (AC-5), not by CI.

Package only runtime files: an ignore rule that keeps dist/ and package.json and drops src/, test/, bench/, node_modules, tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts, build.mjs and package.mjs. The renderer and main bundles are self-contained (overlay/build.mjs bundles react/react-dom and web/src), so no node_modules ship.
package:win must run the existing build first so a stale dist/ can never be packaged.
I1 holds: this stage adds no settings, preferences or configuration surface to the overlay bundle, and does not touch overlay/src/ at all.

The 1600-line diff budget exists ONLY to absorb package-lock.json churn from one new devDependency. Hand-written diff (package.mjs + package.json + README + test) must stay under ~400 lines; if the lockfile alone pushes the total past the budget, stop and route to pm rather than hand-editing the lockfile.
Existing tests may be EXTENDED, never deleted or skipped. No network in tests.
Branch frontend/TASK-215-S1-<slug>. A literal role/... branch is refused by completion proof #4.

Issue #145 is the PARENT of three stages. Write 'Refs #145' in the PR body, never 'Fixes #145': a closing keyword on a stage PR closes the parent while the other stages are unshipped, and this packet preconditions on issue_state: open, so that closure blocks its own dispatch. Observed 2026-08-04 — PR #147 (S2) closed #145 with S1 and S3 not started. Only TASK-215-S3, the last stage, closes #145.
forbidden_actions: Editing anything under overlay/src/ or overlay/build.mjs
Adding an icon/rcedit/win32metadata step, a code-signing step, or an installer (NSIS/Squirrel) — a folder plus exe is the deliverable
Running the packager inside a required check
Adding a settings/preferences file or window to the overlay (I1)

acceptance_criteria.text: overlay/package.mjs exists, uses @electron/packager (pinned exact version in package.json and package-lock.json), and exports the constants OUT_DIR, APP_NAME and the relative packaged executable path; importing it does not start a package run.
`npm run package:win` exists in overlay/package.json, runs the build first, and targets platform win32 / arch x64 with asar enabled and overwrite on, writing under overlay/dist-win/.

overlay/test/packageWindows.test.ts pins the artifact contract: APP_NAME === 'PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay', the packaged path resolves to dist-win/PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay-win32-x64/PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay.exe, and the resolved packager options set no icon and no win32metadata (so no rcedit/wine dependency).
A test asserts the ignore rule excludes src/, test/, bench/, node_modules, build.mjs, package.mjs, tsconfig.json and vitest.config.ts, and includes dist/ and package.json.

The PR body pastes evidence of ONE real `npm run package:win` run performed by the author: the top-level listing of dist-win/PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay-win32-x64/ showing PoEUpgradeAdvisorOverlay.exe, and the total artifact size. If the packager cannot run in this environment, the stage reports blocked with that output rather than claiming a passing artifact.
overlay/dist-win/ is git-ignored (or otherwise proven untracked): `git status --porcelain` after a package run shows no artifact files.

overlay/README.md documents the packaging step, the artifact contract (directory + exe name) and the note that packaging downloads the Electron win32-x64 binary once, and states plainly that packaging/launch.py is what starts this exe for a player.
Both required checks pass; no test was deleted or skipped; overlay/src/ is byte-identical to main.

rollback: Revert the branch; overlay/ returns to build/start/test/typecheck only and no other component references the artifact yet.
